author: reek
body: The settings panel is what DiffusionApp draws its whole left column from, and what ItemDesignerApp, CallPage and WorkflowHtml build their forms with. Nothing had ever asked it what it renders.

author: reek
body: A panel is the wrong thing to grade by eye. Every field kind lowers to a widget carrying a payload -- a gauge carries a value and a maximum, an input carries its text, a button carries its label -- and the payload is where a wrong answer hides. So this chapter walks the built tree and prints the payload of every field, rather than counting nodes.

author: reek
body: The spec below is DiffusionApp's own shape: two dropdowns (one with a selection, one without), sliders, numbers, a toggle, a heading and a separator. Four extra rows are here to ask questions DiffusionApp does not: a slider whose value sits at its maximum, a slider whose lower bound is zero, a second separator, and an id that no field carries.

author: reek
body: The kind name alone cannot fail informatively -- every field kind that lowers to a gauge prints "gauge" whatever numbers it holds. The payload is the assertion.

author: reek
body: A field's widget sits at child 1 of its labelled row, and the row sits two past the panel's title and title separator.

author: reek
body: A text and a number field are wrapped with their error label, so the input is one level deeper than a dropdown or a gauge.

author: reek
body: Thirteen fields, a title and a separator above them.

author: reek
body: A dropdown with no selection must say so rather than naming an option, and one built with a selection must name that option. Both directions, because a trigger that always printed the placeholder would look identical to one that always printed the first option on the other row.

author: reek
body: A gauge fills value over maximum. A value above its own maximum is therefore a fill past the end of the widget, and the GPU renderer does not clamp it, so this is asked as its own question.

author: reek
body: The width field is the one the form validates, and an untouched field withholds its message, so this error must be empty. It is printed because an error label that was never empty would show up here and nowhere else.

target: section:The rows that are not rows
author: reek
body: A separator and a heading lower to a bare widget rather than a labelled row, so they are read at the top level. There are two separators in this spec on purpose: a widget identifier is what every lookup in the tree keys on, so two of them answering to one name is worth printing.
